Everything here is second-hand: re-check addresses and byte patterns against the cited source before you rely on them. ## 1. Safety rules (all devices, never skip)

Titles only; full text in [AGENT-RULES.md](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/AGENT-RULES.md).

- **A1** Do not touch the bootstrap/bootloader or the updater section. [doc]
- **A2** Know the recovery path before anything is flashed. [doc]
- **A3** Back up first. [doc]
- **A4** Never power off during an upgrade. [doc]
- **A5** BOOTSTRAP UPGRADE is the only irreversible step [doc]
- **A6** Verify every candidate image before it is written [doc]
- **A7** First run of a new DSP/audio build: volume down. [doc]
- **A8** Gate what you ship. [doc]
- **A9** Respect transfer limits. [doc]
- **A10** Mods can be mutually exclusive by OS version. [doc]
- **A11** Rehearse recovery with a stock file before the first modified flash [hw]
- **A12** One change per flash. [doc]
- **A13** Gate DSP code against hardware rules the emulators cannot see. [doc]
- **A14** Check the size margin at every loader stage, not just the file size. [hw]
- **A15** Leave the panel-MCU blob, its updater and section 8 (Outbox 8 firmware) stock [doc]
- **A16** Withdraw builds that lose sound. [hw]
- **A17** In the startup menu never press TRIG 2 or TRIG 3 by habit [doc]
- **A18** "Not hardware-tested" must travel with the file. [doc]
- **A19** Red-team your own safety gate. [doc]
- **A20** The progress bar is not proof. [doc]
- **A21** Upload over USB without auto-commit, then commit explicitly. [hw]
- **A22** Never touch an FPGA bitstream or its configuration path [doc]
- **A23** "Success! Rebooting" is not proof. [doc] [hw]
- **A24** Keep private card data above the MmcFs guard and above `0x800000`; [doc]
- **A25** Guard each block, not the average (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A26** On DT2, publish to reply words 670-676 only. [hw]
- **A27** Analog Heat +FX: change only section 3 (MAIN OS), and keep custom code below `0x40206000`. [hw]
- **A28** Code you copy into SHARC memory at run time must be written back from the data cache before it runs. [hw]
- **A29** Leave a trail the ColdFire can read when the DSP stops. [hw]
- **A30** Keep the container under `0x200000` bytes and section 2's table version stock. [doc]
- **A31** A negative is only as good as the search that produced it. [doc]
- **A32** Store each section the way the original stores it. [doc]
- **A33** Never store a DAG register through its own DAG, and keep SIMD data moves where stock has them. [hw]
- **A34** On ColdFire-audio devices (Syntakt, Digitakt mk1, Digitone mk1), the audio interrupt is the budget. [hw]
- **A35** Budget SHARC code with silicon costs, not instruction counts. [hw]
- **A36** The startup-menu recovery listens to DIN MIDI only, on every Elektron box documented here. [hw]
- **A37** A busy share is not headroom (DT2/DN2 SHARC). [hw]
- **A38** If the OS carries a copy of the bootstrap, no patch may touch that copy or the check that triggers it (A4 MK1, Rytm MK1, Machinedrum). [doc]
- **A39** Never let a USB control transfer (EP0) data stage be a whole multiple of 64 bytes on the ColdFire USB controller with stock's driver. [hw]
- **A40** Qualify any startup change after a long power-off, not only after quick restarts or in the emulator. [hw]
- **A41** Disassemble what you assemble. [hw]
- **A42** ColdFire is not a full 68000: check every addressing-mode combination against the ColdFire manual, not against the emulator. [hw]
- **A43** A cave is free only after it survived a hard run on the unit. [hw]
- **A44** A load governor acts on sustained load, never on one block that is already over. [hw]
- **A45** Keep the end of every SHARC hardware loop in 48-bit ISA (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A46** Keep a decoded section 7 under `0xfffff` bytes, and count the decoded size, not the stored one (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A47** Before a stock storage command, check the card is idle; never assume the stock driver times out (DN2, likely DT2). [hw]
- **A48** Find out what is cached from the OS's own start-up, not the bootstrap; keep hot-path accesses to uncached memory few and word-sized. [hw]
- **A49** Test the first install on a unit in stock condition, not only on the developer's unit. [hw]
- **A50** Go through stock's own input paths; never post into its internal queues or overwrite state another core reads. [hw]
- **A51** Run a long soak before a release, and mask every counter to its register width. [hw]
- **A52** Keep per-sample DSP accesses out of external DDR (DT2/DN2). [hw]
- **A53** Use only addresses the unit decodes after the OS has set up its memory map. [hw]
- **A54** Unload a module only while nothing uses it, and give the loader a way out of its own recovery state. [hw]
- **A55** Do not switch the USB mode at run time in anything you ship until it has passed a long switch loop on a unit; prefer asking the user to set the mode in the menu. [hw]
- **A56** On the Octatrack, ColdFire time added to the frame interrupt can cause or cure a DSP stall by a few microseconds either way, so an A/B that only adds or removes a module is not evidence about that module. [hw]

## 3. Recovery and flashing

- [doc] Two upgrade paths: from within the OS (Transfer, DROP page, confirm with YES on the device; devices whose OS does not fully support Transfer are sent to the LEGACY OS UPGRADE page) and from the Startup Menu (device's MIDI port, not USB; hold FUNC while powering on; TRIG 4 = OS UPGRADE; Transfer in LEGACY OS UPGRADE mode). `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#67684a45`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:28](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L28))
- [doc] "Some upgrades also upgrade the bootstrap" right after the first restart; do not turn the power off then. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#065677fb`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:29](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L29))
- [doc] Downgrading is not supported and is at the user's own risk; user content may be lost. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} {elektron-dn2-notes} (`recovery#258d6d79`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:30](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L30))
- [doc] Digitakt II, first reboot after upgrading to OS 1.15: a file-system integrity check (up to a minute). On errors: back up all projects and samples with Transfer, SETTINGS > SYSTEM > FORMAT +DRIVE (tick SAMPLES), re-import. `[doc]` {elektron-dt2-notes} (`recovery#00f8aff4`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:31](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L31))
- [doc] Heat +FX: in-OS path is SETTINGS > SYSTEM > OS UPGRADE with the file sent through MIDI In or USB MIDI In; the startup path takes MIDI In only. `[doc]` {elektron-heat-fx-notes} (`recovery#2a7bab5e`, [hardware/common/recovery.md:32](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/blob/master/hardware/common/recovery.md#L32))

## 7. Open tests and tasks you could settle

- **H5** (stock) Overbridge rejects a modified OS whose container version field differs from stock (shown on the DN2, Digiwerk OB01). Test: No new flash needed if you already have builds: does Overbridge connect to a build whose version field was changed, and to one where it was kept?
- **H18** (stock) The Heat +FX answers the screen request (RPC framing `F0 00 20 3C 10 00`), as the Heat MKII does, so its screen can be mirrored and read without a mod. Test: Open Elek View (bluesgl.github.io/Elek_View) with nothing else on the MIDI port, select the unit, Start.
- **H16** (build) Heat +FX builds need a cold-start test like other ColdFire units: a startup change can pass quick restarts and fail after minutes off (A40). Test: For the next startup-touching build: power off for 10 minutes before judging.
- **H17** (build) Code costs on the Heat +FX follow the DT1's ColdFire lessons (EMAC mode switches, D16 hot-path hooks), since both run audio on an MCF5441x ColdFire. Test: Measure an audio-ISR hook with and without a MACSR switch per block.
- **T10** (needs unit, effort M) Port a DMA-timer load probe (digihealth / A4 0011-style) to the Heat +FX and measure all FX on
- **T11** (needs files, effort S) Unpack the MKI and MKII OS files: sections, container, CPU (peripheral census), any DSP section
- **T12** (needs files, effort M) Compare FPGA bitstreams across devices (sizes, SHA-256, header) and the OS code that talks to them. Leads: on the Rytm MKII, sample bit reduction is a command word sent to the external audio hardware, not PCM work on the ColdFire; and three bitstreams are exactly 54,664 bytes - Heat +FX section 1, A4 MKII section 1, and the Digitone mk1's (inside section 7, loaded by the second CPU)

Report results with the [test-result issue form](https://github.com/70b185/Aggregat/issues/new?template=test-result.yml).
